rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken Cantonese equivalent of “because.”

example.english: I didn't go out, for it was raining.
example.jyutping: ngo5 mou5 ceot1 gaai1 jan1 wai6 lok6 gan2 jyu5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something intended for a person, or for a stated use when 用 is understood or added.

example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 man4 gin6 hai6 bei2 nei5 ge3

rows.note: Use this when the purpose is to benefit, please, or honor B rather than simply to give something to B.

example.english: I only did this for you this time.
example.traditional: 我今次為咗你先至咁做。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 ci3 wai6 zo2 nei5 sin1 zi3 gam2 zou6

rows.note: Use this for movement or development in the direction of B, including an undesirable eventual outcome.

example.english: The situation is heading for the worst outcome.
example.traditional: 件事向住最壞嘅結果發展。
example.jyutping: gin6 si6 hoeng3 zyu6 zeoi3 waai6 ge3 git3 gwo2 faat3 zin2

rows.note: Use this aspect-and-duration pattern to state how long an action or situation has lasted; Cantonese does not normally add a separate word corresponding to for.

example.english: I have worked at this company for five years.
example.traditional: 我喺呢間公司做咗五年。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 ni1 gaan1 gung1 si1 zou6 zo2 ng5 nin4
